thread.title: Midday Update: Wall Street Overcomes Labor Market Miss with Apple at Record High

title: Midday Update: Wall Street Overcomes Labor Market Miss with Apple at Record High
text:
Midday Update: Wall Street Overcomes Labor Market Miss with Apple at Record High May 04, 2018, 01:02:21 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
With help from Apple ( AAPL ) and technical support at the 200-day moving averages, Wall Street's major market averages recovered from their post-jobs sell-off and disappointment over U.S./China trade negotiations to trade sharply higher at midday on Friday. Led by gains in the technology sector, the Nasdaq Composite is set to close the week higher, while the Dow and S&P 500 are still in the red for a second week.
Selling erupted before the open when the monthly labor market report missed consensus estimates with a 164,000 gain in non-farm payrolls and anemic 0.1% increase in hourly earnings, both of which overshadowed a 17-year low in the unemployment rate of 3.9%.
As losses mounted for the Dow and S&P 500, the Nasdaq was gaining altitude with Apple at a record high thanks to reports of Warren Buffett's recent acquisition of 75,000 shares of the tech giant. The index rose to a five-day high and pushed into the green for the week. The Dow and S&P finally caught up to the Nasdaq with the assistance of support at their respective 200-day moving averages and gains in consumer stocks.
European bourses closed higher for a sixth straight week in tandem with gains in the U.S., quarterly results from Ferrari ( RACE ) and a weaker euro and British pound. The British currency fell to its lowest level since January and traded below its 200-day moving average for the first time in a year as the likelihood for the Bank of England to hike UK interest rates this summer is priced out of the currency.
Crude oil was up $1.18 to $69.61 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.01 to $2.72 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $1.30 to $1,311.50 an ounce, while silver was up $0.01 to $16.46 an ounce. Copper was unchanged at $3.08 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 1.92% to $14.09 with the United States Natural Gas Fund was down 0.63% to $22.17. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 0.16% to 22.66 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.03% to $124.24. The iShares Silver Trust was up 0.10% to $15.48.
